text.content:
Embraced by the infernalist Archbishop Sangris in one of the most elaborate Creation Rites Montreal's Sabbat had ever witnessed (Cardinal Strathcona himself attended), Ezekiel rose from his grave a changed being — his youthful innocence replaced overnight by a dark, magnetic intensity. Raised by the Librarians and later forced into the Black Hand by his own sire (who hoped Hand discipline would protect his overly ambitious childe from demonic influence), Ezekiel earned a fearsome reputation destroying Chicago elders during the Sabbat-Lupine-Camarilla war before returning to testify at Sangris' trial. He watched his sire convicted of infernalism and apparently burned alive, and has since dedicated himself to leading the Sabbat back to the glory of the Anarch Revolt, believing the archdiocese of Montreal to be his birthright. Now returned at the head of his pack 25:17 — young, disciplined crusaders rather than mindless rebels — Ezekiel has gathered the open support of the ultra-violent Les Orphelins and the Wretched, and the secret backing of New York's Disciples of the Black Brood (led by his own progeny Christafarious Black), positioning himself as the third and most dangerous contender for Montreal's archdiocese against Archbishop Valez and Bishop Alfred Benezri.

Ezekiel has the body of a sixteen-year-old boy, lithe and strong, his face a disquieting mix of adult experience and childhood innocence, his dark eyes and skin at once alluring and intimidating. What Ezekiel does not know is that his own ambition is quietly driving him down the same infernal path that destroyed his sire — a truth Sangris, now trapped inside the body of the inquisitor DeSoto, desperately wants to prevent, even as Ezekiel rejects any contact from the man he believes to be his sire's executioner. Pierre Bellemare, secretly an agent of the demon Metathiax, has meanwhile made himself Ezekiel's ally, hoping to corrupt the young Serpent utterly.

To most of Montreal's Sabbat, Pierre Bellemare is a lethal, simple-minded biker-gang ruffian who leads Les Orphelins, a pack of orphaned neonates descended from a common sire, Louis le Monstre, whose only surviving original member is Bellemare himself. In truth, Pierre is a dedicated infernalist and secret acolyte of the demon Metathiax, using the pack's very predictability as violent street muscle as cover for a patient campaign of corruption, spreading disease-tainted vitae through the pack's signature Rite of Charybdis (the "Whirlpool"). At Metathiax's direction, Bellemare has been ordered to corrupt Ezekiel, Sangris' childe, and has cheerfully made himself the young Serpent's ally toward that end, all while manipulating the fractious politics of the Queens of Mercy, the Shepherds, and the Quebec Tremere to keep Montreal's vampires distracted from his true work.

Pierre dresses in black leather and rides a Harley, his massive tattooed arms and bald head hidden behind dark glasses; a pistol tattooed on his right palm and index finger is his calling card, aimed at victims with a whispered "Bang. You're dead." He has his finger on the pulse of the entire city — he knows of Archbishop Valez's hesitation, Ezekiel's ambition, and the Shepherds' hubris — and only the growing rebellion within his own pack seems to escape his notice.

Once the Camarilla Prince imposed on Montreal after a Sabbat facade fell over the city in 1760, Strathcona was slowly drawn into the Sabbat's orbit by the Shepherds of Caine, who recognized him as a potential ally; by 1837 he was a full Sabbat sympathizer, and the Shepherds engineered a populist French-Canadian revolt that let him openly break with the Camarilla for good. As archbishop, Strathcona oversaw the construction of Montreal's vast communal haven and its network of catacombs beneath what is now Dorchester Square, using the cholera epidemic of 1832 (secretly caused by the demon Metathiax) as cover to expand the project into one of the largest underground cemeteries in North America, and kidnapping the Camarilla Toreador architect François Dumas to design its centerpiece, the Temple of Eternal Whispers.

Now a cardinal overseeing Montreal from a position of influence beyond the archdiocese itself, Strathcona personally selected and sponsored Carolina Valez as archbishop after the fall of the infernalist Sangris, staking his own reputation and power on her success. He stands to lose the most should Valez fail to hold the city, and quietly keeps agents watching both her and the rising Ezekiel, ready to intervene — even to have Valez destroyed outright as a martyr — should the power struggle threaten to unravel Montreal, the oldest Sabbat bastion in North America.

A Tzimisce blood-scholar and Librarian, Marie-Ange Gagnon was once a member of La Belle Mort, a nomadic European pack that recruited new bloodlines into the Sabbat by force, destroying any Kindred who refused and letting her drink their blood; she was the sole survivor when her pack was decimated during the Chinese Boxer Rebellion, and returned to her birth city of Montreal to join the Librarians, where she began an intimate relationship with fellow scholar Béatrice L'Angou. In 1996, disturbing visions led Marie-Ange to explore the burned-out ruins of the Snake Pit, Montreal's destroyed Setite temple, where she discovered the unconscious body of a man she believes to be the infernalist Sangris, supposedly destroyed in 1992. She has hidden him in her lair ever since, determined to unravel the mystery of his survival and strange vitae.

What Marie-Ange does not know is that her mysterious guest is the possessed inquisitor Santiago DeSoto, his soul entangled by the demon Metathiax, and that her fascination with his darkness is slowly corrupting her Noddist scholarship and drawing her away from Béatrice, who has noticed the distance but not its cause. Marie-Ange is beefy and rugged with black hair, favoring practical work attire, and uses Vicissitude to bring her veins to the surface of her skin, giving her the look of a pulsating road map.

Raised in idle luxury among Montreal's Golden Mile elite, Sébastien Goulet joined the gay-specific nomadic coven the Mattachine after it settled in Montreal's emerging gay district in the 1950s. When most of the Mattachine abandoned Montreal in 1969 to join the Stonewall Riots in New York and never returned, Sébastien remained behind and founded his own coven, the Queens of Mercy, which has controlled the city's Gay Village and its 12,000-15,000 mortal residents as a private feeding ground ever since, migrating its lair from bar to bar as fashions change (currently the club Heaven).

The Queens of Mercy have suffered heavy losses in the past decade — a member's defection to the Wretched, three members slain by Pierre Bellemare, and the unexplained disappearance of Christien Ng — leaving the coven down to just three members, including Sébastien himself. Despite this, the Queens back Alfred Benezri's bid for the archdiocese, giving the Shepherds' candidate crucial support beyond the scholarly Librarians, and their destruction would both undermine the Shepherds and hand an advantage to Ezekiel's chaos-courting faction.

Metathiax is the demon lord imprisoned beneath Mount Royal, a fiend of disease whose presence has poisoned the mountain for centuries — it caused the cholera epidemic of 1832 that Cardinal Strathcona exploited to expand Montreal's communal haven, and it has claimed at least six Cainites in the mountain's train tunnel and eleven more on its slopes over the decades, along with countless native mortals whom Frère Marc has fruitlessly Embraced in the mountain's cemeteries hoping to understand the killings. Sabbat and Shepherds alike shun the mountain, sensing an ominous, watching presence beneath its ancient trees, though few grasp the full truth of what sleeps there.

When Sangris engineered his escape from execution, his soul fled into the body of his inquisitor executioner, Santiago DeSoto, and Metathiax has since contested the demon Bothothel's claim on that soul, negotiating with DeSoto's fractured spirit to trade Sangris' soul back to Bothothel in exchange for a substitute: the soul of Cedilia of the Tongue. Metathiax has since assumed a physical form on Earth, fooled the Shepherds and the Inquisition into believing the island's infernal taint died with Sangris, and manipulated Marie-Ange Gagnon into unknowingly sheltering the confused, possessed DeSoto while its schemes play out.

Bothothel is a Decani plague-lord who once rode a wave of smallpox to exterminate the native population of Hispañola and claimed dominion over a temple in the island's hinterland. There, centuries ago, the vampire Sangris — then a member of the Cult of Legba seeking aid against the Setites — struck a bargain with the demon, agreeing to spread a new corruption, the "plague" of ambition, in exchange for infernal power, secretly intending that Bothothel's ultimate prize would be his own soul only if he failed to find an escape from the pact.

Sangris did find an escape, weaving a Thaumaturgical rite into his own flesh that let his soul flee into the body of his executioner, the inquisitor Santiago DeSoto, at the moment of his apparent destruction in Montreal. Bothothel now contests possession of Sangris' fugitive soul with Metathiax, the demon imprisoned beneath Mount Royal, and has implanted DeSoto's possessed, fractured mind with the subconscious knowledge that Pierre Bellemare is a potent infernalist — a card Bothothel may yet play to further its own ends in the struggle over Montreal.

Cedilia of the Tongue was the priestess of disease who served the demon Bothothel in his temple in the hinterlands of Hispañola, and it was she who first taught the young vampire Sangris the ways of the Decani, setting in motion the infernal bargain that would eventually make him Archbishop of Montreal and, later, a divided soul trapped between two competing demons. Cedilia's exact fate is not detailed, but her significance persists: when the demon Metathiax negotiated with the fractured, possessed soul of Santiago DeSoto to redirect Bothothel's claim away from Sangris, it proposed Cedilia's own soul as the substitute payment, meaning DeSoto (in his search to fulfil his bargain with both demons) may yet be sent hunting for her across the world.

Zhou was a Taoist member of the Shepherds of Caine who applied the principles of feng shui to Sabbat lore, concluding that Montreal's spiritual "ley" lines were mobile rather than fixed, save at stationary nexus points such as Saint Joseph's Oratory and Notre-Dame Basilica — and that when two such lines crossed, disaster inevitably followed those caught at the intersection. Using the ramblings of the deranged Librarian Jacob the Glitch to map where the island's ley lines had crossed and would cross again, Zhou pursued his research into the Sabbat's own Inquisition, serving as the Shepherds' allotted judge inquisitor (the coven is permitted only one knight or judge inquisitor at a time). Zhou was recently destroyed in the line of that duty, leaving the Shepherds' seat within the Inquisition vacant and his feng shui research on Montreal's spiritual geography unfinished.

Born in 1860, Alice Ménard fell at age five into the clutches of Kyle McConner, a pedophile Brujah antitribu who abused her for over a year and used Vicissitude to remake her into a living porcelain doll before finally Embracing her, keeping her bound to him as a plaything into the 20th century. The Nosferatu antitribu Raphael Catarari recognized the beautiful soul buried beneath her torment and helped her grow strong enough to free herself; in 1911 she broke the Vinculum binding her to Kyle and destroyed him in a Monomacy duel hampered by his own twisted affection for her. Raphael brought her into the Shepherds of Caine and onto the Path of Nocturnal Redemption as "Cherubim," the coven's "war-doll."

Cherubim still keeps the leather mask Kyle wore while violating her, and the specter of her abuser haunts her still: during her Divine Tide's ebb, she seeks vengeance through a twisted game of seduction aimed at mortal men, drawing out the pedophile in them before tearing out their hearts at the point of climax. She and Raphael have since begun an intensely sexual relationship that Cherubim fears is merely another man using her as Kyle once did, forcing her to suppress a killing frenzy at the height of their encounters.

Maria Sandoza survived the legendary El Paso battle of 1970 in which Grand Inquisitor Dominion Julian and his corrupted former Black Hand mentor destroyed one another, and assumed the office of Grand Inquisitor herself in 1973, ruling the six judge inquisitors and six knight inquisitors of the Sabbat's small but formidable crusade against infernalism from a secret headquarters rumored to lie in the mountains of northern Mexico. Under her tenure, the once-strict limits on the Shepherds of Caine's influence within the Inquisition have quietly eroded — Sandoza is a close personal friend of Alfred Benezri, and the Shepherds' Path of Nocturnal Redemption has grown steadily more popular among the Inquisition's rank and file, including many of its researchers, templars, and watchers who have become Martyrs sympathetic to the coven's cause.

Sandoza's closeness to Benezri, largely unremarked upon within the Inquisition itself, gives Montreal's Shepherds an unusually direct line to the sect's most feared institution — a fact that could prove decisive if Benezri's bid for the archdiocese ever draws formal Inquisitorial scrutiny, for good or ill.

A skilled Assamite antitribu warrior and politician of the Black Hand, Dominion Julian recognized by 1911 that the first Sabbat Inquisition — by then hopelessly entangled in the sect's civil-war politics under the Shepherd Soeur Jeanne — had to be replaced. Working with Alfred Benezri, he designed a smaller, independent crusade answerable to no faction, and the two men agreed that Jeanne herself had to be sacrificed to legitimize it; the Shepherds watched in silence as she and her followers fell to the Hand outside Philadelphia in 1919. Five years later Julian formally abandoned his Black Hand position (which many believed destined for the rank of seraph) to lead the reformed Inquisition himself, a betrayal for which the Hand branded him a traitor and which he survived twelve separate assassination attempts to escape.

Julian served as grand inquisitor from 1924 until 1970, when he led an attack on a corrupted Black Hand cell in El Paso, Texas, and found himself face-to-face with his own former mentor; the two Assamites destroyed one another in a battle still spoken of with awe. His office remained contested for three years until his subordinate and El Paso survivor, Maria Sandoza, finally claimed it in 1973.

Priscus Gustav Mallenhaus founded the very first Sabbat Inquisition in 1804 after personally encountering demon cultists in Europe, and it was Montreal's Shepherds of Caine — already renowned for their expertise in guarding against demonic incursion — whom he approached for aid and advice in establishing the crusade. Alfred Benezri and several of his covenmates rode with the first Inquisition war party at Mallenhaus' side, cementing a bond between the Shepherds and the Inquisition that has endured, in one form or another, for two centuries. When the fledgling institution matured, command passed to the Shepherd Soeur Jeanne, beginning the long and often troubled relationship between Montreal's oldest coven and the sect's crusade against its own heretics.

Soeur Jeanne was Saint Ignace's most beloved childe and one of the founding lights of the Shepherds of Caine, but when her sire departed the world in Sainting, she refused to abandon her growing duties as head of the first Sabbat Inquisition to return to coven life, throwing the Shepherds into a period of leaderless confusion. Jeanne's Inquisition served the sect well for decades, but by 1900 had degenerated into the political morass of the Sabbat Civil War, its fifty inquisitors hunting political rivals as often as genuine infernalists. Recognizing the institution's corruption, Dominion Julian of the Black Hand and Alfred Benezri quietly designed its replacement and agreed that Jeanne herself would have to be sacrificed to legitimize the new, independent crusade; the Shepherds watched in silence as she and her followers were destroyed by the Black Hand outside Philadelphia in 1919, a betrayal that allowed the coven to weather the closing days of the civil war but has never been openly discussed since.
